title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting: X is a smooth algebraic scheme over a field k that is abstractly isomorphic to C, with no isomorphism chosen. (1) The algebraic de Rham cycle class map P_alg : Cl^p(X) -> H^{2p}(X, Omega^._X) = H^{2p}_dR(X/k) is defined intrinsically over k. It is k-rational and needs no embedding. (2) An isomorphism sigma : k -> C gives the complex manifold X_sigma. The topological cycle class P_top : Cl^p(X) -> H^{2p}(X_sigma, Z) can then be composed with the comparison map 'can' (marginal note: can = de Rham + comparison, i.e. H^{2p}(X_sigma,Z) -> H^{2p}(X_sigma,C) = H^{2p}_dR(X/k) ⊗_{k,sigma} C, the last step by Grothendieck's algebraic de Rham theorem). Since k ≅ C via sigma, the de Rham group is itself a C-space, so H^{2p}(X_sigma,Z) mod torsion sits in it as a lattice E_sigma. This gives P^{(p)}_sigma, which factors through E_sigma. (3) Key relation: P^{(p)}_sigma = (1/sigma^{-1}(2 i pi))^p P_alg. The topological class is the algebraic de Rham class divided by the p-th power of the element of k that sigma sends to 2 pi i. This is the period (2 pi i)^p, i.e. the Tate twist Z(p) = (2 pi i)^p Z. (4) Consequence: sigma^{-1}(2 pi i) varies wildly with sigma, because automorphisms of C move the transcendental pi arbitrarily. So the map P_sigma, and the integral lattice E_sigma inside the k-rational de Rham group, depend strongly on sigma. Example: p=1, X=P^1, where the cycle class is an isomorphism Z -> H^2(P^1,Z). There E_sigma = (1/sigma^{-1}(2 pi i)) · k-line of P_alg(point), which visibly moves with sigma. (5) NB: replacing sigma by its complex conjugate changes 2 pi i into -2 pi i, hence changes P_sigma, with consequences for the lattices E^i_sigma = H^{2i}(X_sigma,Z). Purpose: to show that the Betti integral structure is not an algebraic invariant of X/k. Only the twisted lattice (2 pi i)^p H^{2p}(X_sigma,Z) relates canonically to de Rham classes of cycles. This motivates Tate twists and the comparison of realizations in the theory of motives and Hodge theory.
errors: Complex conjugation changes the factor (1/sigma^{-1}(2 pi i))^p by (-1)^p, not by -1. 'Changes P_sigma into -P_sigma' is correct only for p odd. Here p=1 is the running example, so it is harmless.
In the later formula the factor is written 1/sigma(2 i pi). It should be 1/sigma^{-1}(2 i pi): 2 pi i is in C, so one needs its preimage in k. This is a notational slip.
Superscripts drift between E^{2i}, E^{2p} and E^i. The intended lattice is E^{2p}_sigma = image of H^{2p}(X_sigma,Z).

ideas.what: Algebraic de Rham cycle class compared to the topological cycle class through the comparison isomorphism, differing by (2 pi i)^p
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of cycle classes with the Betti–de Rham comparison; Tate twist Z(p) = (2 pi i)^p Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (algebraic de Rham, 1966); Deligne (Hodge II/III; Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982)
ideas.where_published: Algebraic de Rham comparison in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966). The explicit twist discussion is mainly in Deligne's work.

ideas.what: Dependence of the integral Betti lattice inside de Rham cohomology on the choice of embedding sigma: k -> C
ideas.modern_name: Non-algebraicity of the Betti structure; conjugate varieties / absolute Hodge setting; period torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (absolute Hodge cycles, 1982); Serre (conjugate varieties with non-homeomorphic analytifications, 1964)

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard working note on why the topological integral structure depends on the embedding, via the period 2 pi i (Tate twist). It is consistent with, and earlier than, Deligne's absolute Hodge framework, but contains nothing not well established in the literature.
transcription_corrections: The formula reads P^{(p)}_sigma = (1/sigma^{-1}(2 i pi))^p P_alg, with sigma^{-1} explicitly written.
The bracket in line 2 is plausibly '[de façon non précisée]' rather than '[et de façon non canonique]'.
The inserted note above 'D' is roughly 'π change tout[?] ...', referring to sigma moving π.
The left margin reads 'can = De Rham + Comp' (comparison isomorphism).
